stem: During admission, a nurse identifies a wound on a client's lower leg. Which documentation is most appropriate?

options.A: Record the wound stage and a photograph only; measurements and drainage characteristics can be added at discharge.
options.B: Record the dressing type and pain score only because wound-bed and surrounding-skin findings are treatment rather than assessment data.
options.C: Delay the baseline description until the first scheduled dressing change so admission findings do not affect later comparisons.
options.D: Record the wound's precise location, size, wound-bed and periwound findings, drainage characteristics, pain, and other relevant assessment findings.

rationale: NCBI Nursing Skills states that wound assessment and documentation should include the anatomic location, wound type and degree of tissue damage, wound bed, wound size, wound edges and periwound skin, signs of infection, pain, and drainage characteristics. Wounds should be measured on admission and at subsequent dressing changes so progress can be compared over time. Therefore D is correct. A omits key baseline measurements and drainage findings, B incorrectly excludes wound-bed/periwound assessment, and C delays information needed for comparison and care planning.
educational_objective: Document a wound comprehensively at baseline using precise location, measurements, wound-bed/periwound characteristics, drainage, pain and other relevant findings so later assessments can be compared accurately.
source_organization: NCBI Bookshelf / Open RN Nursing Skills
source_version_date: Current NCBI/Open RN Nursing Skills content live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: 20.3 Assessing Wounds: assessment/documentation includes anatomic location, wound type, tissue damage, wound bed, size, edges/periwound skin, signs of infection and pain. Type and Amount of Exudate: document color, consistency and amount. Wound Size: measure on admission and every dressing change. Checklist for Wound Assessment repeats location, dimensions, drainage, periwound, pain and infection findings.
source_claim_supported: Comprehensive baseline wound documentation should include precise location, dimensions, wound-bed/periwound findings, drainage, pain and other relevant assessment characteristics, with measurements beginning on admission for later comparison.

correction_summary: Retained the comprehensive wound-documentation construct and key D. Tightened the keyed option to specify drainage characteristics and baseline assessment purpose; no difficulty change was needed.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current NCBI/Open RN Nursing Skills wound-care guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.exact_locator: 20.3 Assessing Wounds, Wound Size, Exudate, Periwound, Pain and wound-assessment checklist
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the source-specified wound-assessment components and admission measurement requirement without inventing a particular staging system or photograph requirement for all wound types.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because stage/photo alone omit required baseline dimensions, wound-bed/periwound and drainage findings.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because wound-bed and periwound findings are core assessment/documentation data.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because wounds should be measured on admission rather than delaying baseline assessment.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only D provides a sufficiently comprehensive baseline wound assessment for subsequent comparison.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are documentation strategies for the same newly identified wound.
audit_findings.blueprint: Basic Care and Comfort — wound assessment, comfort/pain and documentation.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current NCBI wound-assessment components, admission measurement guidance, all alternatives, rationale, objective, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN Basic Care and Comfort mapping. D remained uniquely correct.
